I am 60 years old and have farmed this 2 mu in Quzhou for 40 years. I never went to school, but I know this land with my hands and my eyes. My household has 7 people, and some of my children work in the city and send a little money home, so I have some cash for inputs but not much extra labor. We have a well for irrigation, which is our lifeline because rain alone is never enough on the North China Plain.

I grow wheat in winter and maize in summer. That is what everyone in my village does, and it keeps us fed. In early October, I will sow my full 2 mu with improved wheat seed — about 30 jin per mu — that I buy from the village supply shop. The new varieties yield better than the old seeds my mother used. Before planting, I spread one 100-jin bag of compound fertilizer per mu and till with the rotary machine my nephew brings over. I irrigate three times: once before winter so the wheat survives the cold, once in spring when it turns green and starts growing fast, and once when the grain is filling. In spring I also topdress with about half a bag of urea per mu when the wheat is jointing. If the wheat looks yellow I might add a bit more, but urea is expensive so I do not go overboard. I spray for weeds once and for insects once or twice if I see aphids. I expect about 900 jin per mu this year if the weather is normal.

Right after I harvest the wheat in early June, I plant maize on the same 2 mu. The window is only a few days and the soil is already prepared, so I do not till — I just sow directly to save time and moisture. I buy hybrid maize seed, Denghai or Nongda, about 2 jin per mu. I put compound fertilizer in the rows at planting and then topdress with urea when the plants are knee-high. I irrigate twice: once after sowing to help the seeds sprout, and once when the tassels come out if the rain does not come. I spray herbicide once and insecticide once or twice. I expect about 1,000 jin per mu. This is what I have always done and what my neighbors do. On a small plot like mine, I cannot afford to take risks with new methods.
